attempted_claim: On Omega=((-1,1)x(0,pi))\{x=0} consider the singular critical Grushin system dt f - dx^2 f - x^2 dy^2 f + (mu*/x^2) f = 0 with fixed explicit Hardy-range coupling mu*=1/8, equipped with the bridging self-adjoint realization that transmits across {x=0} (Friedrichs-type extension with explicit transmission conditions at the singularity) and homogeneous Dirichlet conditions on the outer boundary, controlled only by Dirichlet data u(t,y) on the single lateral side Gamma={x=1}x(0,pi) and L^2 initial data. Decide whether there exists a finite sharp threshold T*>0 depending only on Omega and mu* such that null-controllability from Gamma holds if and only if T>T*, and determine the exact value of T* when it exists. A complete answer proves the positive boundary observability estimate for every T>T* and falsifies uniform observability for every T<T* by an explicit singular-adjoint concentrating sequence.
claim_type: exact minimal-time threshold with singular potential
decisive_failure: The positive-side uniform-in-n observability estimate with sharp constant at the Hardy-critical bridging singularity was not proved, so the sharp if-and-only-if threshold remains undecided; numerical rate checks are finite-difference corroboration only, not proofs of the observability bounds.
